title: Monitoring Robustness and Individual Fairness

problem.claim: Deployed automated decision-makers should remain robust to slight input perturbations, including in settings involving adversarial or semantic robustness and individual fairness.

gap.claim: Existing fixed-radius nearest neighbor methods lack suitable online solutions for monitoring input-output robustness.

contributions.claim: A runtime-monitoring approach observes one long execution sequence of a deployed black-box AI model and alarms when similar past inputs produced dissimilar outputs.
Clemont provides lightweight monitors, including upgraded online FRNN variants and a monitor based on binary decision diagrams.
An efficient parallelization technique reduces computation time for monitors using the L∞ norm to measure input-output-pair distances.

stated_novelty.claim: One Clemont monitor uses a novel algorithm based on binary decision diagrams.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a comparative study of Clemont monitors on standard benchmarks covering adversarial robustness, semantic robustness, and individual fairness.
The authors report that the monitors effectively detected robustness violations at runtime.
The authors report that the parallelization technique can substantially reduce monitor computation time for L∞-based distance measurements.

narrative_sequence.summary: Robustness to slight input perturbations is desirable in automated decision-making and appears in several literature-defined forms.
The paper proposes runtime monitoring of deployed black-box models by comparing similar past inputs and their outputs.
The monitoring task is formulated as fixed-radius nearest neighbor search, for which suitable online solutions are lacking.
Clemont implements lightweight monitors, a binary-decision-diagram-based algorithm, and parallelization for selected distance computations.
A comparative benchmark study reports runtime detection of robustness violations.

source_observation.claim: The monitoring problem can be reduced to fixed-radius nearest neighbor search, and parallelization helps for L∞-based distances.

interpretation.claim: Algorithmic choices for online similarity search and distance computation materially affect monitoring cost.

application.claim: When implementing runtime monitors, prioritize online nearest-neighbor methods and parallel execution paths suited to the selected distance metric.

exception.claim: The reported parallelization benefit is limited in the abstract to monitors using the L∞ norm.

unknowns: Quantitative detection results and computation-time reductions are not reported.
Benchmark identities, datasets, monitor thresholds, and evaluation protocols are not specified.
False-positive behavior, scalability limits, and deployment conditions are not described.
